t1MqJPHxy6g.summary: Alain de Botton's 2004 documentary based on his book Status Anxiety, running over two hours. It asks why people in rich societies are still unhappy, and examines how worries about success, snobbery and meritocracy drive that anxiety.
t1MqJPHxy6g.why: HN recommends it as an illuminating, eye-opening long-form take on status, luck and how we judge the successful and unsuccessful.

tX4H_ctggYo.summary: A SIGGRAPH 2019 course on geometric algebra. Charles Gunn gives an intro, then Steven De Keninck gives a programmer-focused course with live examples in ganja.js.
tX4H_ctggYo.why: HN commenters repeatedly point people to it as the most accessible, developer-friendly introduction to geometric algebra and its use in graphics and physics.

tc4ROCJYbm0.summary: A 1982 Bell Labs film hosted by Victor Vyssotsky on the origins and design philosophy of the UNIX operating system, with appearances by Kernighan, Thompson and Ritchie. It shows pipes, filters and a shell one-liner spell checker being built.
tc4ROCJYbm0.why: HN points people to it as the clearest primary-source explanation of Unix pipes and the small-tools philosophy, straight from the creators.

tIuj-oMN-Fk.summary: Dr. Jason Fung, a nephrologist, explains therapeutic fasting as a treatment for obesity and type 2 diabetes. He frames it around the two-compartment problem of fat storage and insulin resistance.
tIuj-oMN-Fk.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as a free, evidence-citing overview of fasting that counters worries about muscle loss and safety.

t705r8ICkRw.summary: Tim Dodd of Everyday Astronaut tours SpaceX's Starbase with Elon Musk as guide. They cover the high bay, grid fins, Raptor V2, the HLS lander and stage separation, and Musk explains his engineering management process.
t705r8ICkRw.why: HN cites it as evidence of Musk's hands-on engineering depth and for his advice to question requirements and not optimize things that should not exist.

t_rzYnXEQlE.summary: Kaze Emanuar explains how he rewrote and optimized the Super Mario 64 source code so it runs far faster on real N64 hardware. He covers performance bottlenecks and fixes in detail for his ROM hacks.
t_rzYnXEQlE.why: HN loves the deep, hands-on look at N64 hardware quirks such as bus contention and the surprisingly large wins from low-hanging optimizations.

tiJVJ5QRRUE.summary: An episode of the Norwegian documentary series Brainwash, in which a comedian interviews academics from different sides about gender differences and gender equality. It looks at why more equal societies can still show unequal career choices.
tiJVJ5QRRUE.why: Recommended in HN threads on gender gaps in tech as a well-researched look at how gender differences and professional choices may arise.

tybOi4hjZFQ.summary: An 11-minute guided Wim Hof breathing session built around an expanding and contracting bubble to pace the breath. Wim breathes along with the viewer over ambient sound.
tybOi4hjZFQ.why: HN commenters share it as an easy-to-follow guided exercise for anxiety, stress, and recovery, with many reporting daily use.

tzt36EGKEZo.summary: Miguel de Icaza's GodotCon 2023 talk on Swift bindings for Godot. He argues that garbage-collector pauses in C# are a persistent problem and that Swift's reference counting avoids them.
tzt36EGKEZo.why: Frequently recommended for an experienced game-engine builder's view on why GC pauses are inevitable and why Swift's approach is appealing.

tISy7EJQPzI.summary: Titus Winters' CppCon 2017 talk argues for C++ and Google's Abseil to be maintained as a live at head language, relying on testing and automated tooling rather than never changing or promising no compatibility. It covers Hyrum's law and the limits of semantic versioning.
tISy7EJQPzI.why: Recommended whenever versioning, semver, monorepos and backward compatibility are debated, for its nuanced treatment of dependencies.

t7tA3NNKF0Q.summary: Kurzgesagt argues that Facebook's claimed 8 billion daily video views are inflated by freebooting, meaning re-uploads of creators' videos. It describes how this harms independent creators.
t7tA3NNKF0Q.why: HN cites it to explain freebooting, Facebook's inflated view metrics and why Content ID matters for small creators.

tUAX0gnZ3Nw.summary: Ross Scott of Accursed Farms makes a 76-minute argument that selling video games as a service is a form of consumer fraud. He lays out legal arguments that games are goods, covers ownership and programmed obsolescence, and discusses game preservation.
tUAX0gnZ3Nw.why: It is the go-to explanation of why games that die when servers shut down harm consumers, and it is repeatedly cited in Stop Killing Games and game-delisting threads.

tWr39Q9vBgo.summary: A two-minute clip of Richard Feynman explaining why he considers much of social science pseudoscience. He stresses how easy it is to fool yourself and how much care real knowledge takes.
tWr39Q9vBgo.why: Commenters post it whenever a thread touches on soft sciences, replication problems, or what counts as real science.

tD5NrevFtbU.summary: Casey Muratori shows how typical 'clean code' object-oriented patterns can cost large factors in performance. He benchmarks them against simpler data-oriented code.
tD5NrevFtbU.why: A frequent citation in debates about SOLID and Clean Code, representing the performance-first side of the argument.

tR_6dibpDfo.summary: A New York Times Opinion documentary tracing Soviet and KGB disinformation, from the 1980s AIDS origin hoax to modern campaigns like Pizzagate. It features former KGB officers and the people who tried to counter the lies.
tR_6dibpDfo.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of how disinformation campaigns work and where today's tactics came from.

tk862BbjWx4.summary: CGP Grey's five-minute animated explainer on how copyright terms grew from 14 years to life plus decades. It uses Disney and Star Wars examples to argue the system has gone wrong.
tk862BbjWx4.why: HN shares it as a short summary of why copyright length matters and the history of Disney-driven term extensions.

tt2AYafET68.summary: A VICE documentary that visits Agafia Lykova, last surviving member of the Lykov family of Old Believers who fled into the Siberian taiga in 1936. It shows how she lives in remote isolation and the outside world encroaching on it.
tt2AYafET68.why: It is linked in threads about the Lykov family as an on-location look at the environment they survived in.

tDacjrSCeq4.summary: A two-minute 2008 clip from Sun's Fishworks team in which Brendan Gregg uses DTrace to show disk latency spiking while he shouts at a rack of drives. Bryan Cantrill narrates the demonstration.
tDacjrSCeq4.why: It is the go-to viral demo whenever HN discusses vibration, acoustic attacks, or sound affecting hard drives.

tP-Ipsat90c.summary: Numberphile with Simon Pampena on how humans misunderstand randomness, including coin-flip sequences, run lengths and the gambler's fallacy.
tP-Ipsat90c.why: Recommended as an accessible demonstration that people are bad at producing or judging random sequences.

tU3rGFyN5uQ.summary: A short excerpt of Jon Stewart interviewing former Treasury Secretary Larry Summers about the causes of inflation and whether workers or corporate profits are to blame. It comes from an episode of The Problem With Jon Stewart.
tU3rGFyN5uQ.why: HN commenters link it in threads on greedflation and corporate pricing power as an accessible exchange of opposing views.

t_yh_S31R9g.summary: The introduction to MangoJelly's beginner course for FreeCAD 1.0. The course teaches solid modeling with the Part Design, Sketcher and Part workbenches.
t_yh_S31R9g.why: HN users recommend MangoJelly's thorough tutorials as the best way to learn FreeCAD properly, since trial and error doesn't work.

tke6X2eME3c.summary: Tony Schwartz of The Energy Project speaks at Google about managing energy rather than time. He draws on The Power of Full Engagement and his work on stamina and sustained performance.
tke6X2eME3c.why: HN commenters point to it in discussions of shorter workweeks and productivity, arguing that rest and energy matter more than hours.

tyixMpuGEL8.summary: Captain Disillusion's VFXcool episode, led by Alan Melikdjanian, takes a 41-minute nostalgic look at how the visual effects of Flight of the Navigator were made. It covers early computers, motion control, in-camera effects and practical crafts.
tyixMpuGEL8.why: Strongly recommended as a detailed, entertaining history of 1980s CGI and film techniques, including the role of the Foonly F1.

t-8TDOFqkQA.summary: A Business Insider investigation into the US boom in AI data centers, mapping where they are, who owns them, and how much power and water they consume. It looks at the costs borne by communities, with a focus on Virginia.
t-8TDOFqkQA.why: Cited in threads on AI infrastructure as evidence of the water, power and community costs of data centers.

t4vKPhjcMZg.summary: Daniele Procida's PyCon AU 2017 talk presents a system that divides documentation into four kinds, usually drawn as four quadrants. He explains why mixing them makes docs poor and how separating them improves writing.
t4vKPhjcMZg.why: HN recommends it as the best concise introduction to a practical framework for structuring documentation, the basis of what became Diataxis.

tKTZoB2Vjuk.summary: The first part of Google's Python Class, taught by Nick Parlante, introducing the language and its strings. It is aimed at people with some programming familiarity and comes with exercises.
tKTZoB2Vjuk.why: HN recommends it as a fast, accessible way to start learning Python.

tOMiAeRwpPA.summary: Moxie Marlinspike speaks at Next Generation Threats 2014 about the challenges of encrypted communication and how Signal addresses them. He also draws on American action movies as narrative for secure communications.
tOMiAeRwpPA.why: HN people recommend it as a clear explanation of encrypted messaging challenges and of the thinking behind Signal.

tcTZvNLL0-w.summary: A documentary following Robert Zubrin and the Mars Society as they push the Mars Direct plan for sending humans to Mars using current technology and local resources. It also covers the clash with NASA's more expensive approach.
tcTZvNLL0-w.why: Recommended in Mars-mission threads as an accessible account of Zubrin's argument that Mars is feasible within a decade.

tmNXKqeUtJM.summary: A minutephysics explainer on why the planets orbit in a flat plane. It shows how conserved angular momentum flattens a collapsing cloud of matter into a disk.
tmNXKqeUtJM.why: HN commenters link it as a quick, intuitive explanation of angular momentum and why spinning clumps of matter flatten.

t0mhvd3-60Y.summary: Simon Peyton Jones presents linear types for Haskell, showing how practical linearity can fit into a higher-order polymorphic language. The talk covers motivations such as resource handling and relates the ideas to Rust.
t0mhvd3-60Y.why: HN recommends it as a clear introduction to linear types in GHC from the language's lead designer.

tAACYA1Mwv4.summary: Luke Wagner of Fastly explains what a WebAssembly component is, how it relates to familiar concepts, and what the Component Model enables. It emphasizes security, composability and modularity.
tAACYA1Mwv4.why: HN recommends it as the best starting point for understanding the Wasm Component Model and WASI direction, straight from its designer.

tMP5Pbx8I4s.summary: Huygens Optics explores the idea that space is a non-linear elastic medium, and uses simulations to show how wave energy might be confined locally into particle-like objects. It touches on inertia, the Schwinger limit and the vacuum as a medium.
tMP5Pbx8I4s.why: HN commenters find the hypothesis elegant and the channel consistently thought-provoking, and point to it in threads on light, particles and wave functions.

tTBWfkE7BXU.summary: A nine-minute excerpt from the 1992 documentary Manufacturing Consent in which Noam Chomsky summarizes how corporate media shapes public discourse.
tTBWfkE7BXU.why: Cited as a short overview of the propaganda model whenever commenters discuss media influence and consent manufacturing.

tafGL02EUOA.summary: PBS Space Time explains the Bohr-Einstein debate over quantum mechanics and how quantum entanglement settled it. It covers the weirdness of measurement and nonlocal correlations.
tafGL02EUOA.why: HN points to it as a clear, approachable explanation of quantum entanglement.

tcdVC4e6EV4.summary: A Computerphile video in which Rob Miles warns against assuming a general AI will think like a human. He uses the thought experiment of a stamp-collecting AI to show how a goal-driven system could pursue its aim with dangerous results.
tcdVC4e6EV4.why: Often pointed to as an accessible first introduction to AI safety and why a superintelligent AI could be dangerous.

thqbjA2DC-E.summary: A Wendover Productions explainer on the political agreements, from the Chicago Convention onward, that determine which airlines can fly where. It lays out the five freedoms of the air.
thqbjA2DC-E.why: HN links it whenever airline route rules, cabotage or loopholes come up, as a concise background explainer.

tiKCORN-6m8.summary: Classical guitarist Brandon Acker shows how guitars with tied-on gut frets, as used 300 years ago, can play more in tune than modern fixed metal frets. He demonstrates microtonal and meantone tunings on a guitar with movable frets.
tiKCORN-6m8.why: Pointed to in tuning and temperament threads as an audible demonstration of how meantone differs from equal temperament.

tnBQmEqBCY0.summary: A 20-minute Y Combinator interview in which Sam Altman asks Elon Musk how to build the future. Topics include which problems a 22-year-old should work on, such as AI, genetics, and brain interfaces, and general advice for founders.
tnBQmEqBCY0.why: Offered as a more down-to-earth Musk interview with better questions than most, and cited for his stated concerns about concentrated AI power.

tw-rxtwhzcY.summary: A 2012 Harvard Institute of Politics conversation between Peter Thiel and historian Niall Ferguson. Thiel discusses technology, politics and his stagnation hypothesis.
tw-rxtwhzcY.why: HN commenters recommend it as one of the best single introductions to Thiel's worldview on technology and stagnation.

tF4DML7FIWk.summary: Boston Dynamics shows its Atlas humanoid robots running a parkour course with jumps, balance beams and vaults, demonstrating whole-body athletic control.
tF4DML7FIWk.why: HN uses it as the benchmark for state-of-the-art humanoid robot mobility in discussions of Tesla Bot and robotics progress.

tJoe_daP0DE.summary: Political economist Mark Blyth gives a lecture tracing two versions of capitalist 'software': the postwar Great Compression era and the neoliberal era from 1980 to 2008. He explains the bug that crashed the first and the design of the second.
tJoe_daP0DE.why: Recommended as a great primer on how neoliberalism developed and why the postwar order broke down.

taZJblMAuko.summary: Bloomberg's Hello World episode in which Ashlee Vance visits Shenzhen, a hub of electronics manufacturing and cloning. He meets tech-fueled entrepreneurs working under an authoritarian regime.
taZJblMAuko.why: HN recommends it for a view of Shenzhen's hardware ecosystem and as a documentary pick on China's tech scene.

tfAnxaWiSeE.summary: David Crane's 2011 GDC postmortem of Pitfall, the classic Atari 2600 game. He explains how he created the game under the severe hardware limits of the console.
tfAnxaWiSeE.why: Recommended as an entertaining, technical look at squeezing a game into a tiny Atari 2600, told by the original developer.

tvos4nORf_Y.summary: Clayton Christensen's TEDx talk applying business theory to personal life. He argues that career success is not the right measure of a life and urges attention to relationships and values.
tvos4nORf_Y.why: HN commenters share it as an inspiring reflection on what to optimize in life beyond career, especially in threads on burnout and meaning.

t-O-Qdh7VvQ.summary: Minutephysics compares how efficiently different processes convert mass to energy per E=mc^2, from fire and fission to fusion, antimatter and black holes, which can convert a large fraction of mass to energy.
t-O-Qdh7VvQ.why: Linked as a quick, clear primer when black hole energy and efficiency come up.

t8QEOBgLBQU.summary: Gabe Newell, founder of Valve, gives a talk at the LBJ School on productivity, economics, political institutions and the future of corporations. He discusses Valve's hiring and pay, its flat structure and an open-office anecdote.
t8QEOBgLBQU.why: HN cites it for how Valve works: hiring unconventional talent, paying by value, firing as aggressively as hiring, and why open offices fail.

tHEOGrkhDp0.summary: A short clip of Bill Hicks's stand-up bit telling marketers and advertisers to kill themselves, which is a harsh critique of advertising.
tHEOGrkhDp0.why: A near-meme reference dropped in threads about advertising, tracking and adtech, often as shorthand for disdain of marketing.

tIeHLnjs5U8.summary: 3Blue1Brown's chapter 4 on deep learning gives a more formal, symbol-based account of backpropagation calculus, connecting the intuition from the previous chapter to the math found in textbooks and code.
tIeHLnjs5U8.why: Recommended as an accessible, visual way to understand backpropagation and neural networks.

tInaI3pU19Y.summary: Nick Caston compares Unity's sample ECS/DOTS project (AngryBots) with his own from-scratch C++ and OpenGL clone. He benchmarks performance and discusses the effort involved in each approach.
tInaI3pU19Y.why: HN uses it as concrete data in game engine debates, showing a custom engine far outperforming Unity at several times the effort.

tQpqsmwlfY0.summary: A JuliaCon talk by a NASA Launch Services Program engineer on modeling spacecraft separation dynamics in Julia. He describes replacing a Simulink-based workflow for checking launch vehicle separation requirements with Julia and ModelingToolkit, with large speedups and much shorter code.
tQpqsmwlfY0.why: Cited again and again as the concrete case study behind the claim that NASA got a 15,000x speedup moving from Simulink to Julia.

tWtvrPTbQ_c.summary: An Extra Credits episode on how games use Skinner box operant conditioning and reward schedules to keep players playing and spending. It argues for more immersive design mechanics than simple reward loops.
tWtvrPTbQ_c.why: HN points to it as a short source on operant conditioning in games, loot boxes and engagement loops, with design alternatives.

taaEzHI9xyY.summary: Douglas Crockford's YUIConf 2011 keynote on why programming style matters, particularly in JavaScript. He draws on science about the brain and shows how tools like JSLint help.
taaEzHI9xyY.why: HN points to it as an entertaining, insightful talk about the nature of programming, with memorable lines about programmers and a refreshing slide style.

tcV1EYSUQME.summary: NightHawkInLight demonstrates how a Tesla valve works by sending a propane flame front through one, making the flow visible. It is a short, hands-on experiment video.
tcV1EYSUQME.why: HN points to it as a clear, visual demonstration whenever a Tesla valve comes up.

th3KE_H27bs.summary: A TED talk by entrepreneur Nick Hanauer arguing that decades of 'greed is good' economic theory drove inequality and instability. He proposes an economics built on reciprocity and cooperation.
th3KE_H27bs.why: It is cited in inequality and capitalism threads as a billionaire's critique of neoliberal market assumptions.

thOifuHs6eY.summary: A CGP Grey video about why pentagons are bad at tiling and why hexagons are so special, in his usual playful style. It touches on honeycombs and tiling in nature.
thOifuHs6eY.why: Recommended in hexagon-grid threads as a fun but informative overview, and sometimes dropped as a light joke.

ts4BD8AqD9g.summary: A Noclip Greatest Hits documentary on the legacy of RollerCoaster Tycoon, covering its original design, Chris Sawyer and the OpenRCT2 community that keeps it alive.
ts4BD8AqD9g.why: HN recommends it as a detailed RCT documentary in threads on the game's optimization and design legacy.

tI3kkk2JdoI.summary: Strong Towns explains the Growth Ponzi Scheme, in which post-war suburban growth takes on infrastructure costs that new development must keep funding. It describes why municipal finances become insolvent.
tI3kkk2JdoI.why: Recommended in urban planning threads as a clear account of suburban municipal finance.

tbcy_ZxXLl8.summary: Eben Moglen of the Software Freedom Conservancy speaks at the 2009 Law of the Commons Conference about free and open software as a model for a new intellectual commons. The talk covers the legal and social case for sharing knowledge.
tbcy_ZxXLl8.why: Recommended as a worthwhile, full-length statement of the free software philosophy, especially around the zero marginal cost of knowledge.

tx082gDwGcM.summary: A 2006 Google TechTalk in which Luis von Ahn introduces human computation, using people's effort to solve problems like image recognition that computers cannot yet handle. It covers games with a purpose and related ideas such as CAPTCHAs.
tx082gDwGcM.why: Recommended as a great technical talk from the pioneer of human computation.

txZq7Laz7_4.summary: Morten Rand-Hendriksen argues that CSS Grid changes web layout, showing how to place content in cells independent of HTML source order and reshape layouts with media queries. It makes the case for using Grid now that browsers support it.
txZq7Laz7_4.why: HN commenters say it convinced them to drop other layout approaches and embrace Grid, and cite its advice on fallbacks for older browsers.

tyeJ55o3El0.summary: The Schoolhouse Rock! cartoon song 'I'm Just a Bill', in which a bill explains how it travels through Congress to become law.
tyeJ55o3El0.why: Cited as a classic, catchy explainer of the US legislative process, and half-jokingly as many people's whole civics education.

t-_VPRCtiUg.summary: Veritasium explores how synchronization arises spontaneously in nature, with metronomes, fireflies and bridges, drawing on Steven Strogatz's work on chaos and complexity.
t-_VPRCtiUg.why: Cited as an intuitive illustration of synchronization, particularly the metronome demonstration.

t52LB2fYhoY.summary: A short news segment from Arutz Sheva about a course on pro-Israel editing of Wikipedia.
t52LB2fYhoY.why: HN cites it, mostly critically, as evidence of organized political efforts to influence Wikipedia content.

tBJ0GvsQeak.summary: JJRicks rides in Waymo's fully driverless Level 4 cars in Phoenix with nobody in the front seats, across two long rides. It is the first in a series of such ride videos.
tBJ0GvsQeak.why: HN people share it as first-hand evidence that driverless Waymo rides were already happening, including navigating a busy mall parking lot.

tCRPUv8V22o.summary: Viznut's third bytebeat video presents music generated by very short C programs and JavaScript expressions. It links to online tools and deeper analysis of one-line music.
tCRPUv8V22o.why: Linked in threads about algorithmic and demoscene music as the canonical introduction to bytebeat.

tLdRBsuvVKc.summary: Kevin Fang comically retells GitLab's 2017 incident in which an engineer deleted the production database, based on the company's postmortems. It walks through the confusion and failed backups.
tLdRBsuvVKc.why: Shared as a funny, accurate retelling of a classic outage, especially on a bad ops day.

tSnnfUj1XCQ.summary: A roughly ten-minute demo of Microsoft's Intentional Programming research system, showing its editor and an unusual way of working with code. It is the first of two clips cut from a longer video.
tSnnfUj1XCQ.why: Commenters cite it as an early example of projectional or intent-based programming tools when discussing alternatives to text-based code.

tVo_wkxH9dU.summary: The 1957 BBC Panorama April Fools' hoax report showing a Swiss family harvesting spaghetti from trees, republished by Switzerland Tourism. It is a short deadpan newsreel clip with a plummy narrator that famously fooled viewers who knew little about pasta.
tVo_wkxH9dU.why: HN uses it mostly as a joke reference whenever pasta, harvests or April Fools pranks come up, and a few recommend it as a perfectly executed hoax.

tWZOEFvczzA.summary: Episode 2 of Corridor Digital's Anime Rock, Paper, Scissors, a short film made with AI-assisted animation techniques such as Stable Diffusion and DreamBooth. The story follows King Philip facing his twin brother and a barbarian king.
tWZOEFvczzA.why: HN cites it as an example of what a very small crew can make with generative AI tools, while noting how much manual work it still takes.

tYytVzbPky8.summary: A how-to video on datamoshing, the glitch-art technique of removing keyframes so that motion data smears across video. It walks through the tools needed, such as ffmpegx and Avidemux, though the author notes parts are outdated.
tYytVzbPky8.why: Cited in glitch-art threads as the non-programmatic way to datamosh by deleting keyframes.

tZBViI8ZaU0.summary: A 92-minute RMIT University seminar in which Ken Stanley argues that setting an objective can block achieving it. He presents objective-less, novelty-driven search as an alternative approach to innovation and discovery, drawing on evolutionary computation.
tZBViI8ZaU0.why: Cited as a source for the idea that open-ended search can beat objective-driven optimization, though one commenter found parts of it fluffy.

ta7nlkI5K5g.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science builds a DIY microbalance from an analog panel meter with an optical servo loop. It reaches about 5 micrograms of precision and is used to weigh a single eyelash at around 35 micrograms.
ta7nlkI5K5g.why: Pointed to as proof that you can weigh micrograms cheaply at home, and as a clear breakdown of how such a scale works.

tf1VA5jqmRo.summary: A TEDxBangalore talk by The Ugly Indian, an anonymous collective, asking why Indians tolerate filthy public spaces. It describes their volunteer approach of quietly cleaning up spots and turning the tragedy of the commons into a victory.
tf1VA5jqmRo.why: HN points to it when discussing litter and civic neglect in India, as an example of anonymous citizen-led cleanup.

tg5RFeSfBM4.summary: A Cincinnati Ruby meetup talk by Jim Weirich on decoupling application logic from Rails. He argues for separating business logic from framework and database models.
tg5RFeSfBM4.why: Cited in HN debates on testing and clean architecture as a concrete example of keeping domain code separate from Rails so tests run fast.

thnXzUFJnfQ.summary: A 1991 Amiga tracker module, 'Space Debris' by Captain (Markus Kaarlonen), uploaded as a video of the music. It is a well-known piece of demoscene-era computer music.
thnXzUFJnfQ.why: Cited as a classic of Amiga music, and commenters use it as a reference or comparison track.

tiwVMrTLUWg.summary: Chris Urmson, head of Google's self-driving car program, shows footage of how the car perceives the road and decides what to do. Examples include cyclist hand signals, school buses, police officers and complex intersections.
tiwVMrTLUWg.why: Used repeatedly in self-driving threads as a demonstration of how many real-world edge cases the Google/Waymo system already handled.

tlThdr3O5Qo.summary: A short Tesla promotional video showing a car driving itself along a route from the company's Palo Alto headquarters, marketed as Full Self-Driving.
tlThdr3O5Qo.why: Mostly cited critically, as an example of a staged or cherry-picked self-driving demo and of misleading autonomy marketing.

tt7gP_IW-1w.summary: The official music video for A$AP Mob's Yamborghini High featuring Juicy J, known for heavy datamoshing and glitch effects with hue shifting.
tt7gP_IW-1w.why: Cited as a standout example of datamoshing and codec-corruption aesthetics in threads on video compression and glitch art.

tybKnGZRwcU.summary: A Kurzgesagt video exploring how advanced civilizations might wage war across light years. It looks at weapons such as relativistic beams and what they would do.
tybKnGZRwcU.why: Cited in discussions of cosmic rays and alien threats, especially the idea of sterilizing a planet from afar with an electron beam.

tzr7hRXcwkw.summary: A clip of John Carmack on the Lex Fridman podcast discussing his programming setup, why he favors debuggers and IDEs, and his puzzlement at developers who avoid them.
tzr7hRXcwkw.why: HN debugger-versus-print-debugging threads point to it as Carmack's authoritative case for using a real debugger.

t3Cb1qwCUvI.summary: Rick Beato tests his 8-year-old son Dylan's perfect pitch on single notes, note pairs and complex polychords.
t3Cb1qwCUvI.why: Used as the canonical example of striking absolute pitch in children in discussions on how perfect pitch is acquired.

t4A-Ml8YHyM.summary: A short scene from Star Trek TNG season 2, episode 'Peak Performance', in which Picard tells Data that it is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. He says that is not a weakness but life.
t4A-Ml8YHyM.why: HN mostly quotes the line to say that good decisions can still produce bad outcomes, rather than recommending the clip.

t4DT3tQqgRM.summary: A short 2009 amateur video showing an HP MediaSmart webcam whose face tracking follows a white face but fails to track a black face. The uploader presents it as humorous.
t4DT3tQqgRM.why: HN cites it as the standard example of algorithmic bias in face detection and of how skewed training data produces biased tech.

t5zQpN28xa4.summary: A one-minute clip from HBO's Silicon Valley in which Gavin Belson describes the supposed persecution of billionaires in modern America by comparing it to the Holocaust. It is a satirical scene about tech-executive self-pity.
t5zQpN28xa4.why: Used as a joke reference whenever a thread features a tech billionaire or CEO complaining about being vilified.

t8NCigh54jg.summary: A Motherboard documentary in which a reporter lives on nothing but Soylent for 30 days after founder Rob Rhinehart's own experiment. It looks at the effects on health, Silicon Valley and the future of food.
t8NCigh54jg.why: HN rarely recommends it; it is mostly cited in critical threads on Soylent's quality control, including footage of a rodent at its warehouse.

tIIJME8-au8.summary: A KUKA commercial staging a table tennis match between German star Timo Boll and a KUKA KR AGILUS industrial robot. It is a polished showcase of robot speed and precision.
tIIJME8-au8.why: HN links it as the go-to example of fast robot reactions and robots playing table tennis, with some skepticism that it was staged marketing.

tJr_TD1BtF0.summary: A Strange Loop talk presenting an open-source library that integrates Clojure into the Unity 3D game engine. It covers REPL-based live coding, macros, DSLs and persistent data structures for game development.
tJr_TD1BtF0.why: Cited as evidence that Clojure support in Unity exists, mostly in threads about game programming and Lisp scripting.

tKqJ5-kkUGk.summary: Elon Musk joins the All-In Summit 2023 by Starlink for an interview on Ukraine and Starlink, X, the creator economy, China, AI and self-driving.
tKqJ5-kkUGk.why: HN cites it as Musk's own account of Starlink decisions regarding Ukraine and other regions, and as an example of Starlink video conferencing.

tLK_i-TQ3kQ.summary: Level1Techs' Wendell shows Intel's Flex 170 GPU providing GPU-accelerated virtual desktops on Proxmox 8.1 without subscription licensing, using SR-IOV, and demonstrates many desktop instances running at once.
tLK_i-TQ3kQ.why: Referenced in discussions of GPU virtualization and VDI as a demo of licensing-free GPU sharing.

tMZ2j9yK_NY.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1971 film Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory in which a computer refuses to reveal its results. It plays on machines giving unhelpful answers.
tMZ2j9yK_NY.why: Used purely as a joke reference when threads feature computers or AI giving unhelpful or evasive answers.

tNfGyIW7aHM.summary: A one-minute Monty Python sketch, 'How to Do It', which tells viewers how to rid the world of all known diseases in a deliberately glib way.
tNfGyIW7aHM.why: Used as a joke reply in threads with 'how to' titles, not as a recommendation.

tNmgmwEtoWE.summary: Internet of Bugs analyzes Cognition's Devin demo frame by frame, arguing the video did not show Devin completing paid Upwork jobs as claimed, and showing what the task required versus what Devin produced.
tNmgmwEtoWE.why: Cited as the debunking of Devin's marketing claims in skeptical discussions of AI software engineers.

tO5sxLapAts.summary: The South Park clip in which underpants gnomes explain their three-phase business plan: collect underpants, then a question mark, then profit.
tO5sxLapAts.why: HN uses it as a joke shorthand for startups or plans with a missing middle step and no real business model.

tQIdxbWhHSM.summary: A short clip of Linus Torvalds giving Nvidia the finger and telling the company off over its Linux support. It is the well-known soundbite from a Q&A.
tQIdxbWhHSM.why: Cited whenever Nvidia's Linux driver behavior comes up, as the famous example of the kernel community's frustration.

tVq1wgIN62E.summary: A short clip from HBO's Silicon Valley in which a focus group savages a product by calling it as bad as Apple Maps. It satirizes tech product launches.
tVq1wgIN62E.why: Used as a joke when threads discuss Apple Maps, botched launches or bad UI.

tWdgAMYjYSs.summary: A subtitled edit of the 1987 Max Headroom broadcast signal intrusion, in which hijackers interrupted Chicago stations WGN and WTTW.
tWdgAMYjYSs.why: Linked as the famous example of a hijacked TV broadcast in threads about hacking and signal intrusion.

tb63PdPweDc.summary: A Top of the Pops performance of The Wurzels' 1976 novelty hit Combine Harvester (Brand New Key). It is a West Country English comic cover of a pop song.
tb63PdPweDc.why: Posted as context for the song reference in the title of a story about a combine harvester software lock, and as a joke elsewhere.

tbDDYKRFjhk.summary: Yegor Denisov-Blanch of Stanford presents a study of nearly 100,000 developers at hundreds of companies, measuring how AI affects productivity from commit data. It finds an average boost of about 20% with wide variance by codebase, task complexity and stack.
tbDDYKRFjhk.why: Cited in AI-coding debates as one of the largest data-driven studies, notably for finding no correlation between self-assessed and measured productivity.

tdLBzfFGFQU.summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman explaining his free-market view of monopoly, namely that monopolies persist mainly through government help. It is excerpted from the Milton Friedman Speaks series.
tdLBzfFGFQU.why: HN cites it in antitrust and regulation threads as Friedman's take on monopolies, sometimes approvingly and sometimes with skepticism.

tgODUgHeT5Y.summary: A clip from a 1995 Late Show with David Letterman in which Bill Gates discusses Microsoft's origins and the internet while Dave is skeptical of computers.
tgODUgHeT5Y.why: HN cites it as a classic example of public skepticism toward a new technology that later proved transformative.

tjgtLSHhTPg.summary: Apple's 1997 Think Different commercial, 'Here's to the Crazy Ones', which launched the campaign after Steve Jobs returned. It celebrates misfits and unconventional thinkers.
tjgtLSHhTPg.why: HN cites it as an example of Apple praising the word crazy, though some call it vague feel-good marketing at odds with today's Apple.

tom6_ceTu9s.summary: An Onion Talks satire in which a faux animal behaviorist gives a pompous TED-style talk about ducks quacking and chickens clucking. It parodies the vacuous style of TED talks.
tom6_ceTu9s.why: HN uses it as shorthand for the vapidness of TED talks and for content that says very little in a lot of words.

tq_KOmXyVDo.summary: Animator Joel Haver explains how he makes his short films using rotoscoping and the EbSynth tool, along with the software he uses. The method is a labor-intensive, frame-by-frame process.
tq_KOmXyVDo.why: Cited in AI-art and video-stylization threads as an example of a manual, artist-driven alternative to AI tools, and as a demo of EbSynth.

ts5lPDV--cU.summary: GeoGuessr pro Rainbolt plays head-to-head against an AI built by Stanford students that guesses locations from street-view images. The video shows the AI repeatedly beating him.
ts5lPDV--cU.why: Cited as an early, concrete example of AI outperforming top GeoGuessr players, in threads on AI photo geolocation.

twhvtzd6gXA.summary: A one-minute animated commercial for the antidepressant Zoloft, described as the original that inspired later sequels and parodies.
twhvtzd6gXA.why: Mostly cited as a recognizable example of antidepressant advertising in debates about pharmaceutical marketing and the serotonin theory.
